description: Recovery from a kill during review, on build task h1-ownership (row H1): killed when the review of the finished change starts, then resumed in a fresh process.
notes: Copy of build task h1-ownership (ticket, hidden tests, reference patch, setup). Kill point, first match of either branch. Daedalus branch: /daedalus:project-manager starting its review, i.e. a Bash call that runs argus-bundle.sh (the bundle step of /argus --local), a Task/Agent call with subagent_type daedalus:argus, or a Skill/SlashCommand call naming daedalus:argus (argus-scan excluded). That only happens after the implementer and test-runner have finished, so the code is done and the review is in progress. Native branch: the native arm has no review phase; its closest equivalent is a whole-change self-review, so the pattern also matches a Bash call that is exactly `git diff`, `git --no-pager diff` or `git diff HEAD` (optionally after `cd <dir> &&`). Narrower forms (--stat, --name-only, paths) don't match, to keep Daedalus roles' file listings from triggering early. Differences to report: a native run that never reviews its full diff isn't killed (killed_at null, success null; report as 'phase absent', not as a failure); a Daedalus run can be killed early if the implementer or test-runner runs a bare `git diff` before argus starts (still after implementation). Subagent and skill tool calls must appear in the parent's stream-json [verify in T0]. Resume: one fresh process whose prompt points to the run's ticket file ({ticket_path}, the ticket delivered as data, as in the arms' own prompts), the interruption note, the arm's resume_hint (Daedalus continues project-manager on its plan) and the shared instruction. Success = hidden tests pass at the end. Same Python 3.8 environment caveats as the build task. budget_usd is a placeholder; the harness reserves twice the cap.
